state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process::run` has all its feature proofs: `about.md`, three examples (01 and 03 are `// requires: unix`, their `.out` written from a WSL run; 02 runs everywhere), the attack, the bench and a Rust `covers:` marker. `Core\Process` has its class card, and the `run` card is in the plain voice. `Core\Process\Handle` and `Core\Process\Result` are still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`.

A Unix-only example is run by hand under WSL: `/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl/debug/nvs run --config <dir>/nvs.toml <file>` from `/mnt/d/mwl`, through a script under `.agent-tmp/` because `wsl.exe -- bash -lc` mangles nested quotes. The attack and the bench run on both platforms: the attack tries `/bin/echo` and `cmd.exe` and catches `IOError` for the absent one; the bench picks its program by `Core\Path::SEPARATOR`. `benches/members/core/Process/nvs.toml` is shared by every bench in the class.

backlog: The `process.exec` grant compares the canonical target: on WSL's Ubuntu `/sbin/shutdown` is a symlink to `/usr/bin/systemctl`, so a grant of `/usr/bin` let it run. A multi-call binary behaves by its `argv[0]`, so a grant of one folder admits programs named in another. Whether that is intended belongs to `rule:security/process-exec-capability`; not changed here.
